title.narrative: Improving Waste Management and Public Awareness for a Clean and Healthy Ocean (Grenada)

description.narrative: 1. The project is expected to deliver significant socio-economic benefits, enhancing human well-being and resilience in Grenada. By addressing waste and wastewater management, the project will directly contribute to climate security by reducing pollution that exacerbates marine hypoxia and supporting nature-based solutions that strengthen coastal resilience to climate impacts such as storms and sea-level rise. 2. Through improvements in water security, the project will protect critical water resources from contamination, ensuring cleaner and safer access for both human consumption and agricultural use. This is particularly vital in a Small Island Developing State like Grenada, where water resources are limited and vulnerable to climate variability. 3. The project will also enhance food security by safeguarding marine ecosystems that support fisheries, a critical source of nutrition and income for local communities. By mitigating marine hypoxia and promoting sustainable waste management practices, the project will ensure the health and productivity of marine biodiversity, which underpins local livelihoods and food supplies. 4. In terms of health benefits, reducing exposure to polluted water and land-based waste will lower the prevalence of waterborne and pollution-related diseases, particularly in vulnerable populations. Furthermore, the project’s emphasis on sustainable practices will promote cleaner and healthier environments, contributing to improved public health outcomes. 5. The project will bolster the sustainability of livelihoods by creating economic opportunities in waste management, tourism, and agriculture. Capacity-building activities will empower communities and private sector actors with the skills and knowledge needed to adopt sustainable practices, enhancing their economic resilience and reducing vulnerabilities to environmental and economic shocks. 6. The project explicitly integrates Sustainable Blue Economy principles, which prioritize the sustainable use of ocean resources for economic growth, improved livelihoods, and job creation while preserving the health of marine and coastal ecosystems. This approach offers transformative socio-economic benefits by fostering industries such as sustainable fisheries, eco-tourism, and innovative waste management solutions, which create long-term economic value while protecting vital ecosystems. 7. A critical component of the project is fostering behavioral change at all levels, from communities to policymakers and private sector stakeholders. Through targeted awareness campaigns, education programs, and stakeholder engagement, the project aims to cultivate a culture of environmental responsibility. By encouraging the adoption of sustainable practices and reducing reliance on unsustainable waste management behaviors, the project will ensure lasting environmental and socio-economic benefits that extend beyond its lifecycle. 8. By fostering inclusive stakeholder engagement and incorporating gender-sensitive approaches, the project will promote equitable development, ensuring that benefits are shared across all segments of society. This comprehensive approach will reduce vulnerabilities while building long-term socio-economic resilience for Grenada’s communities.
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

To reduce marine hypoxia in Grenada through improved management of nutrient and organic pollution from land-based resources through an integrated approach that combines regulation, awareness raising, stakeholder collaboration, and implementing nature-based solutions, all within the framework of the Sustainable Blue Economy.
